scripted_findings.title: Visitors cannot tell where they are on 9 page(s)
scripted_findings.evidence: https://www.pentagram.com/contact: h1 'Pentagram' is the homepage's h1; https://www.pentagram.com/about: h1 'Pentagram' is the homepage's h1; https://www.pentagram.com/work: h1 'Pentagram' is the homepage's h1; https://www.pentagram.com/news: h1 'Pentagram' is the homepage's h1. A visitor arriving mid-site from an AI answer reads the title and h1 first to confirm they landed in the right place; a page that names nothing, or repeats the homepage heading, gives them no such confirmation.

pages.text_excerpt: Ferrari Yearbook Pentagram Ferrari Yearbook Preview — Mar 13, 2026 Pentagram Partner Domenic Lippa has designed a typographic cover for the car manufacturer‘s 2025 Yearbook. Published in the traditional large format with a hard cover and special papers, The Ferrari Yearbook 2025 retraces the most significant moments of an eventful season for the Italian car manufacturer. The latest in a line of yearbooks dating back to 1949, the new publication celebrates Maranello’s defining moments from the previous 12 months. Pentagram was asked to create a cover for the 2025 Yearbook that was bold and impactful, but continued the legacy of the previous Yearbook designs. pages.text_excerpt: ‘Margaret Calvert: Roadworks’ Pentagram ‘Margaret Calvert: Roadworks’ Preview — Sep 18, 2025 The first show at Pentagram‘s Osh Gallery features new artworks by the renowned designer and typographer. For the first exhibition in Pentagram’s new Osh Gallery, designer, typographer and fellow Islington resident Margaret Calvert will showcase art pieces inspired by the signage designed with Jock Kinneir for the British road network. Described as ‘a pioneer of design for public service’, Margaret has played a defining role in shaping Britain’s visual identity. Her long and prolific collaboration with Kinneir began when she was just 21, working together on signage for the newly opened Gatwick Airport. pages.text_excerpt: Caligra: ‘Computers for Experts’ Pentagram Caligra: ‘Computers for Experts’ Preview — Sep 15, 2025 An exhibition featuring Jon Marshall’s industrial design which runs as part of the London Design Festival 2025. Caligra is a new computer company that's developing a Linux-based operating system called Workbench, and the C100 Developer Terminal hardware that's designed specifically to run it. The C100 has been created in collaboration with Pentagram industrial design partner Jon Marshall. Jon and his team worked closely with Caligra to translate the elements needed for a developer-focused machine into clear, functional hardware design.
